test_title: PYST 03: SSC Stenographer 2025: English Language & Comprehension (Held On: 06 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Arrange the sentence parts:

(A) were injured

(B) many passengers

(C) in the accident

(D) yesterday
solution:
The correct answer is** Option (3)** i.e. **BACD**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence begins with the subject "many passengers," which is correctly indicated by **part (B).**
 
• Following the subject, "were injured" **(BA)** continues the logical sequence, making it clear what happened to the passengers.
 
• **The next part,** "in the accident," indicated by** (C),** provides the context of the injury.
 
• **Ending with **"yesterday" **(D)** completes the sentence by specifying the time.

Therefore, the correct answer is **BACD.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (BCAD):** This option starts with "many passengers in the accident were injured yesterday," which breaks the logical flow and incorrectly structures the sentence.
 
• **Option 2 (BCDA):** This option starts with "many passengers in the accident yesterday were injured," which places the time context too early in the sentence, disrupting coherence.
 
• **Option 4 (BADC):** This option starts with "many passengers yesterday were injured in the accident," which misplaces the time element, creating an awkward sentence structure.
